# University of Jordan
The University of Jordan (UJ) was established in 1962 as the first university in Jordan, following a royal decree by King Hussein bin Talal and Prime Minister Wasfi al-Tal. Located primarily in the Jubaiha area north of Amman, its main campus spans 1,200 dunums and features twelve gates, extensive student parking, and modern facilities. The university also operates a southern branch in Aqaba, established in 2009 as part of a national strategy to expand higher education in the region. Initially operating with limited resources, UJ expanded significantly over the decades, adding faculties such as Medicine, Engineering, and Law, and establishing research centers, a teaching hospital (Jordan University Hospital), and an academic library.
Academically, UJ offers over 200 programs across scientific, humanitarian, and medical faculties, including the School of Engineering, the King Abdullah II School of Information Technology, and the School of Medicine. It is recognized for its research output, having published thousands of papers and patents, and holds a ranking among the top universities in Jordan and the Arab world. The university boasts a diverse student body and a notable alumni network comprising many prominent figures in politics, science, business, and international diplomacy, including former Prime Ministers and diplomats who have served in high-level roles globally.
